for_senior_author: Causal verbs for randomized evidence below high certainty: cl_alc_withdrawal_medicines (low) and cl_alc_naltrexone (moderate) say 'reduced' with relation 'reduces', as project convention allows; second readers 193 and 200 suggested 'may reduce' or noted the reviews' 'associated with'. cl_alc_acamprosate, also randomized, uses 'is associated with' because its own review names bias as a possible explanation. Decide whether low and moderate randomized claims should carry graded verbs ('may', 'probably').

cl_alc_combine_talking_therapy keeps relation 'does-not-detectably-change' for adding the therapy to medicine, now beside a nominal benefit with placebo pills (79.8 against 73.8 abstinent days in 100, P = .04, corrected post hoc, two single groups) and the authors' reading that the therapy helped without naltrexone. A judgment: 'insufficient-evidence' or a narrower claim are alternatives.

Status flags that are judgments: cl_alc_aud_other_medicines is 'replicated' although it gathers several medicines, two with null results; cl_alc_pregnancy_drinking and cl_alc_fasd_fas_prevalence are 'single study' although each rests on one review of many primary studies (shown to readers as 'one study'); cl_alc_withdrawal_delirium is 'replicated' on four placebo groups, one of which (1969) holds 130 of 186 people and 8 of 11 cases.

sc_rosner_2010b: second reader 200 would rate the interpretation gap substantial, not minor (harm result reported in the opposite direction in the plain language summary and Discussion; a null primary outcome demoted after extraction; 'safe' without serious-event data; unverifiable IPD verification). Rating left as minor on the card.

sc_anton_2006: second reader 194 would add to gap (1) that the composite outcome (odds ratios 1.82 to 2.16) and the P=.04 placebo comparison give the abstract's 'fared better' some support; interpretive, not entered.
sc_lange_2017: second reader 199 finds AMSTAR 2 item 6 'yes' generous ('no' defensible); overall rating unchanged.

Carvalho et al. (2019), Figure 1 shades the USA in the 10.1–15.0% band (verified by pixel colour; now key finding [26] on sc_carvalho_2019). Not used in cl_alc_aud_prevalence because the Seminar does not say which survey WHO's US estimate rests on (it may itself be NESARC-III). Decide whether it belongs in the claim as context.

Popova et al. (2017) and Lange et al. (2017): whether the birth-weighted regional and world averages include the meta-analysed country values (South Africa's 585.3 FAS per 10,000 and 111.1 FASD per 1,000 would push the African means well above drinking/67 and drinking/13 unless South Africa carried under 1% of weighted births). Needs appendix table A7 and eTable 4 and outside birth data (second reader 199).

Eight new anchors written by the adjudicator (ai-located, located_by 'AI reader 223 (adjudicator)') need a second reader's targeted check; until then cl_alc_aud_prevalence, cl_alc_withdrawal_delirium, cl_alc_naltrexone, cl_alc_acamprosate, cl_alc_aud_other_medicines, cl_alc_combine_talking_therapy and cl_alc_fas_first_description return to metadata-verified when the patch is applied.
